{"id": "e5e7c8e1-965c-4914-b93d-1bf7fc086041", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I found the likely cause: the security group has no inbound rule for SSH (port 22).

You didn't say which instance, so I checked all three Linux instances in us-east-1. All are named `ssm-skill-test` and are in the same subnet. Only the security group is a problem.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Instance state and status checks | All three running, with instance and system checks passing and no scheduled events. |
| Public IPs | All three have one: `203.0.113.10`, `203.0.113.11` and `203.0.113.12`. |
| Route table | The default route `0.0.0.0/0` goes to an active internet gateway. |
| Network ACL | The default ACL allows all traffic in and out. |
| Security group `sg-a8544cd4` (default) | **The only inbound rule allows traffic from members of the same security group. There is no rule for TCP 22.** |

The network path is fine, but the security group silently drops SSH packets from outside. That is why the connection times out instead of being refused.

Two related points:
- **No key pair:** none of the instances has an EC2 key pair (`KeyName` is empty). Opening port 22 may not be enough unless keys were added some other way, such as user data or an AMI baked with keys.
- **Session Manager:** all three have the SSM instance profile attached. If the SSM agent is online, you may be able to connect through Session Manager without opening any port. I haven't checked whether the agent is registered.

**Fix:** add an inbound TCP 22 rule to `sg-a8544cd4` that allows only your IP or your corporate CIDR, not `0.0.0.0/0`. All three instances share this security group, so the rule would open SSH on all of them. I can make the change once you approve it. I need the source CIDR you connect from, for example `203.0.113.10/32`.

If SSH used to work, someone probably removed a rule from this security group. I can check the audit history to see who changed it and when, if you want that.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
